page-disks.title.disk.note: The toolbar's name of a machine opened from the page's address (not one kept in this browser) with a disk: {{machine}} is the machine's name (e.g. Debian 13), {{disk}} its disk's file name. Also how other tabs name it (a connection or a device it holds).

page-disks.title.noDisk.note: The toolbar's name of a machine opened from the page's address that boots a disk of the user's and has none yet; {{machine}} is the machine's name.

page-machine.noMachine.message: There is no machine {{id}} in this browser.
page-machine.noMachine.note: Detail under “Couldn't open the machine” in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the page's address (`?m=`) names a machine that isn't kept in this browser; {{id}} is the id in the address.

page-machine.noDisk.message: The machine <name>{{name}}</name> has a disk that isn't stored in this browser any more: {{id}}.
page-machine.noDisk.note: Detail under “Couldn't open the machine” in the message bar (under the toolbar) when one of the machine's disks is gone from this browser; {{name}} is the machine's name, {{id}} the missing disk's id.

messages.state.idle.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) and on the plaque in the middle of the screen and the serial terminal when no machine has started yet (a disk to open, a question first).

messages.state.loading.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) when the machine is being prepared: the emulator, its files, a snapshot.

messages.state.booting.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) when the machine runs and hasn't finished booting.

messages.state.running.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) when the machine runs.

messages.state.off.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) and on the plaque in the middle of the screen and the serial terminal when the machine was powered off.

messages.state.suspended.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) and on the plaque in the middle of the screen and the serial terminal when the machine was suspended (its memory kept in this browser).

messages.state.rebooting.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) when the guest asked for a restart.

messages.state.crashed.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) and on the plaque in the middle of the screen and the serial terminal when the guest or the emulator stopped with an error.

messages.state.failed.note: The machine's state in the status bar (inside “The machine: …”, and the page's state for tools) and on the plaque in the middle of the screen and the serial terminal when the machine couldn't start.

StateVeil.resume.note: Button on the plaque in the middle of the screen (and of the serial terminal, when it shows alone) while the machine is suspended, under the word Suspended: it starts the machine again where it was left.

StateVeil.start.note: Button on the plaque in the middle of the screen (and of the serial terminal, when it shows alone) while the machine is powered off, under the words Powered off: it starts the machine.

worker-messages.state.loadingPercent.note: The machine's state in the status bar while the emulator's and the machine's files download; {{percent}} is how much of them has arrived.

messages.progress.note: The machine's state in the status bar during a long job (a disk saved to a file, changes loaded, a snapshot written): {{phase}} is what it is doing (e.g. Writing the snapshot), {{percent}} how far it is.

problems.retry.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the machine couldn't start or stopped (a file missing, the disk in use, no memory): it tries again what failed. After a start it starts the machine again; after a snapshot's restore that failed (the restore itself, or its start before the snapshot loaded) it restores the snapshot again.

serial-terminal.showLog.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the guest's kernel panicked or the emulator failed: it shows the serial terminal (what led to it).

serial-terminal.copyLog.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the guest's kernel panicked or the emulator failed: it copies the serial console's output to the clipboard.

serial-terminal.copyLog.copied.note: What the Copy serial log button in the message bar (under the toolbar) says once the log is on the clipboard.

serial-terminal.copyLog.failed.note: What the Copy serial log button in the message bar (under the toolbar) says when the browser refused the clipboard (Save serial log is beside it).

serial-terminal.saveLog.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the guest's kernel panicked or the emulator failed: it downloads the serial console's output as a file.

problems.resume.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the machine was suspended: it starts the machine again, resuming it where it was.

problems.bootInstead.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the machine was suspended: it asks, then boots the machine from its disk and drops its suspended memory.

problems.bootInstead.confirm.message: Boot the machine from its disk instead? This will discard its suspended memory, and anything the guest hadn't written to its disk will be lost, as after a power cut.
problems.bootInstead.confirm.note: Text of the question asked by Boot instead (the message bar, after a suspend).

problems.bootInstead.ok.note: The confirm button (drawn as a warning) of the question asked by Boot instead.

runner.boot.loading.note: Title of the boot card (over the screen while a machine starts) when it starts from a snapshot file; {{name}} is the file's name.

runner.boot.starting.note: Title of the boot card (over the screen while a machine starts) while its files load; {{machine}} is the machine's name (e.g. AArch64 machine).

worker-messages.boot.booting.note: Title of the boot card (over the screen while a machine starts) once the machine runs and boots; {{machine}} is the machine's name.

worker-messages.boot.kernel.note: Line on the boot card when the machine has just started running, before the guest's own lines replace it.

worker-messages.boot.downloading.note: Line on the boot card while the emulator's and the machine's files download: {{loaded}} arrived so far of {{total}}.

worker-messages.boot.downloaded.note: Line on the boot card while the emulator's and the machine's files download and the server didn't say their size: {{loaded}} arrived so far.

worker-messages.asleep.message: The guest has suspended itself. Press a key or click its screen or terminal to wake it.
worker-messages.asleep.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the guest suspends itself (its own sleep, not the page's Suspend); it clears itself after a while.

trim-actions.trimmed.message: The guest's unused disk space was freed: its disks' changes went from {{before, bytes}} to {{after, bytes}} in this browser's storage.
trim-actions.trimmed.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the Home page's Free unused disk space, when the guest trimmed its filesystems. {{before}} and {{after}}: what the machine's disks' changes took in this browser's storage before and after.

trim-actions.failed.message: Some of the guest's filesystems couldn't be trimmed (the guest's journal says why). Its disks' changes went from {{before, bytes}} to {{after, bytes}} in this browser's storage.
trim-actions.failed.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the Home page's Free unused disk space, when the guest trimmed some of its filesystems and failed for others. {{before}} and {{after}}: what the machine's disks' changes took before and after.

trim-actions.none.message: None of the guest's filesystems can hand back unused space: none is on a disk that takes it.
trim-actions.none.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the Home page's Free unused disk space, when no filesystem in the guest takes a trim (none is on a disk, or the disks don't discard).

trim-actions.noAnswer.message: The guest didn't free its unused disk space: its agent didn't answer.
trim-actions.noAnswer.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the Home page's Free unused disk space, when the guest agent isn't connected or didn't answer in time.

trim-actions.full.message: To make room, the guest freed its unused disk space: its disks' changes went from {{before, bytes}} to {{after, bytes}} in this browser's storage.
trim-actions.full.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the page found the browser's storage full (disks:devices.storageFull) and had the guest trim its filesystems, when that made the disks' changes smaller. {{before}} and {{after}}: what they took before and after.

grow-actions.grown.message: The guest grew <name>{{disk}}</name>: its partition and filesystem now take {{size, bytes}}.
grow-actions.grown.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the guest agent answered the page's ask to grow a disk the Home page resized with "Grow the partition and filesystem at the next start" (disks:ResizeDisk.grow) on, when it grew the disk's last partition and its filesystem. {{disk}}: the disk's name (as the machine's Disks tab names it). {{size}}: the partition's size now.

grow-actions.grownWhole.message: The guest grew <name>{{disk}}</name>'s filesystem to {{size, bytes}}.
grow-actions.grownWhole.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the guest agent answered the page's ask to grow a disk the Home page resized with "Grow the partition and filesystem at the next start" (disks:ResizeDisk.grow) on, when the disk has no partition table and the guest grew the filesystem that fills it. {{disk}}: the disk's name (as the machine's Disks tab names it). {{size}}: the disk's size.

grow-actions.already.message: <name>{{disk}}</name> already fills its {{size, bytes}} in the guest: nothing was left to grow.
grow-actions.already.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the guest agent answered the page's ask to grow a disk the Home page resized with "Grow the partition and filesystem at the next start" (disks:ResizeDisk.grow) on, when the disk's last partition and its filesystem reached the disk's end already (a grow done before). {{disk}}: the disk's name (as the machine's Disks tab names it). {{size}}: the partition's (or disk's) size.

grow-actions.partOnly.message: The guest grew <name>{{disk}}</name>'s last partition to {{size, bytes}}, but not its filesystem
grow-actions.partOnly.note: Headline of a notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the guest agent grew the last partition of a disk the Home page resized (disks:ResizeDisk.grow) but not the filesystem on it; why, and what the user can do, is the cause under it (machine:grow-actions.notMounted, .unsupported, .stacked, .failed, .failedAgain). {{disk}}: the disk's name (as the machine's Disks tab names it). {{size}}: the partition's size now.

grow-actions.notGrown.note: Headline of a notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the guest agent grew neither the last partition nor the filesystem of a disk the Home page resized (disks:ResizeDisk.grow); why, and what the user can do, is the cause under it (machine:grow-actions.badTable, .notLast, .notMounted, .unsupported, .stacked, .failed, .failedAgain). {{disk}}: the disk's name (as the machine's Disks tab names it).

grow-actions.notMounted.message: Its filesystem isn't mounted, and only mounted filesystems are grown. Grow it yourself in the guest (resize2fs, btrfs filesystem resize or xfs_growfs).
grow-actions.notMounted.note: Cause under machine:grow-actions.partOnly or .notGrown (message bar): the filesystem on the grown disk's last partition isn't mounted in the guest, so the agent left it alone.

grow-actions.unsupported.message: Its filesystem isn't ext4, btrfs or xfs, the ones the guest agent grows. Grow it yourself in the guest.
grow-actions.unsupported.note: Cause under machine:grow-actions.partOnly or .notGrown (message bar): the filesystem on the grown disk's last partition is of another type than the agent grows.

grow-actions.stacked.message: The partition holds LVM, encryption or RAID, which are left alone. Grow what's on it yourself in the guest (pvresize, cryptsetup resize, mdadm --grow).
grow-actions.stacked.note: Cause under machine:grow-actions.partOnly or .notGrown (message bar): the grown disk's last partition holds another block device (LVM, LUKS, md), which the agent doesn't grow.

grow-actions.notLast.message: The new space doesn't follow a partition the guest agent grows (an extended partition ends last, or there's none). Partition the new space yourself in the guest.
grow-actions.notLast.note: Cause under machine:grow-actions.notGrown (message bar): the disk's partition that ends last isn't one the agent grows (an MBR extended partition, or a table without partitions).

grow-actions.badTable.message: Its partition table doesn't add up, so it was left as it was. Check it in the guest (gdisk or fdisk), then grow the partition and filesystem yourself.
grow-actions.badTable.note: Cause under machine:grow-actions.notGrown (message bar): the disk's GPT or MBR partition table didn't pass the agent's checks (a CRC, a header, a partition outside the disk), and nothing was written.

grow-actions.failed.message: It failed (error {{errno}}). The guest tries again at the machine's next start.
grow-actions.failed.note: Cause under machine:grow-actions.partOnly or .notGrown (message bar), the first time a grow failed in the guest: the page asks again at the next start. {{errno}}: the guest's error number (Linux errno).

grow-actions.failedAgain.message: It failed again (error {{errno}}), and won't be tried again. Grow the partition and filesystem yourself in the guest (growpart, then resize2fs, btrfs filesystem resize or xfs_growfs).
grow-actions.failedAgain.note: Cause under machine:grow-actions.partOnly or .notGrown (message bar), the second time a grow failed in the guest: the page stops asking. {{errno}}: the guest's error number (Linux errno).

grow-actions.badRequest.message: The guest agent didn't understand the request to grow <name>{{disk}}</name> (it may be older or newer than this page), so nothing was grown. It's asked again at the machine's next start; once the agent and the page agree, the disk grows.
grow-actions.badRequest.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar), once per page load, when the guest agent answered the page's ask to grow a disk the Home page resized (disks:ResizeDisk.grow) by saying it couldn't read the ask: the agent in the guest and the page are of different versions. {{disk}}: the disk's name (as the machine's Disks tab names it).

runner.workerFailed.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the worker that runs the machine failed (the machine has crashed; Show serial log and the like follow); the browser's error is the detail under it.

runner.notStarted.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when something the page prepares before a machine starts (its shared folders, its keyboard layout) failed (Retry follows); the error is the detail under it.

runner.runsElsewhere.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the machine to start already runs in another tab or window (Retry follows): the headline; what to do is the cause under it (machine:main.runsElsewhere.cause); {{name}} is the machine's name.

runner.runsElsewhere.cause.message: It's running in another tab of this web app. Power it off there or close that tab, then <ui>Retry</ui>.
runner.runsElsewhere.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:main.runsElsewhere, on the line under it in the same place; what to do. <ui>Retry</ui> is the message bar's button (machine:problems.retry).

power-actions.cantOpen.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the machine kept in this browser that the page opens is gone, or one of its disks is; why is the detail under it.

power-actions.machines.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after “Couldn't open the machine”: it opens the Home page.

power-actions.restart.confirm.message: Restart the machine? This will power it off immediately, like pulling the plug, and unsaved work in the guest will be lost.
power-actions.restart.confirm.note: Text of the question asked by the toolbar's Restart while the machine runs.

power-actions.restart.now.message: The guest is shutting down or restarting. Restart the machine now? This will power it off immediately, like pulling the plug, and unsaved work in the guest will be lost.
power-actions.restart.now.note: Text of the question asked by the toolbar's Restart when the guest was already asked to shut down or restart (a second click).

power-actions.restart.title.note: Title of the question asked by the toolbar's Restart while the machine runs.

power-actions.restart.ok.note: The confirm button (drawn as a warning) of the question asked by the toolbar's Restart.

power-actions.powerOff.confirm.message: Power off the machine? This will stop it immediately, like pulling the plug, and unsaved work in the guest will be lost. To stop it cleanly, shut down the guest first, for example with the poweroff command.
power-actions.powerOff.confirm.note: Text of the question asked by the toolbar's Power off.

power-actions.powerOff.now.message: The guest is shutting down or restarting. Power off the machine now? This will stop it immediately, like pulling the plug, and unsaved work in the guest will be lost.
power-actions.powerOff.now.note: Text of the question asked by the toolbar's Power off when the guest was already asked to shut down or restart (a second click).

power-actions.powerOff.title.note: Title of the question asked by the toolbar's Power off.

power-actions.powerOff.ok.note: The confirm button (drawn as a warning) of the question asked by the toolbar's Power off.

power-actions.openDisk.prompt.message: Open a disk image to start the machine. It must be an arm64 Linux image that boots through UEFI: qcow2, raw, or an installer or live ISO. Use <ui>Open disk…</ui>, or drop the file on this web app. What the machine writes to the disk is kept in this browser, separately for each file.
power-actions.openDisk.prompt.note: What the message bar (under the toolbar) says on a first visit, when the page's machine has no disk yet; an Open disk… button follows.

power-actions.openDisk.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) on a first visit (the page's machine has no disk yet): it opens the browser's file picker for a disk image.

disk-actions.switch.confirm.message: Open <name>{{machine}}</name>? This will power off <name>{{running}}</name> immediately, like pulling the plug, and unsaved work in its guest will be lost.
disk-actions.switch.confirm.note: Text of the question asked when another machine is opened (the Home page's Open, a disk file opened or dropped) while the one on the page runs. {{machine}} is the name of the machine to open, {{running}} is the name of the machine running in this tab.

disk-actions.switch.title.note: Title of the question asked when another machine is opened while the one on the page runs. {{machine}} is the name of the machine to open.

disk-actions.switch.ok.note: The confirm button (drawn as a warning) of the question asked when another machine is opened while the one on the page runs.

disk-actions.switch.suspend.note: A button between Cancel and Open in the question asked when another machine is opened while the one on the page runs and can be suspended: this machine is suspended (its memory kept in this browser) rather than powered off, then the other opens.

disk-actions.switch.confirm.suspend.message: Open <name>{{machine}}</name>? This will power off <name>{{running}}</name> immediately, like pulling the plug, and unsaved work in its guest will be lost. To continue <name>{{running}}</name> later where you left off, suspend it instead.
disk-actions.switch.confirm.suspend.note: Text of the question asked when another machine is opened while the one on the page runs and can be suspended; its buttons are Cancel, Suspend and open, Open. {{machine}} is the name of the machine to open, {{running}} is the name of the machine running in this tab.

disk-actions.switch.confirm.soft.suspend.message: Open <name>{{machine}}</name>? The guest of <name>{{running}}</name> will be asked to shut down first; you will be able to power it off forcibly, if needed. To continue <name>{{running}}</name> later where you left off, suspend it instead.
disk-actions.switch.confirm.soft.suspend.note: Text of the question asked before opening another machine while this one runs and can be suspended, when its guest's agent (the page's program in the guest) can shut it down cleanly; its buttons are Cancel, Suspend and open, Open. {{machine}} is the name of the machine to open, {{running}} is the name of the machine running in this tab.

snapshot-actions.runsOn.note: Line after the headline of an error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when Suspend failed: the machine wasn't suspended and still runs; why is the detail under it.

memory-signal.lessRam.confirm.message: Start with less RAM? This will orphan the machine's snapshots, as they were taken with its old settings. They remain stored, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
memory-signal.lessRam.confirm.note: Text of the question asked by Start with N MiB of RAM (the message bar, after the machine's tab closed while it ran) when the machine has kept snapshots.

memory-signal.lessRam.ok.note: The confirm button of the question asked by Start with N MiB of RAM when the machine has kept snapshots.

memory-signal.crashed.message:
<name>{{name}}</name>'s tab closed while it was running ({{when}}), most likely because the browser ran out of memory. The emulator counted about {{gib}} GiB in use ({{peak}} GiB at most), with {{ram}} MiB of guest RAM and a {{jit}} MiB JIT cache.
A smaller JIT cache keeps less of the guest's code compiled; when the cache is full, the browser uses about six times its size for it. Less RAM leaves the guest less room.
memory-signal.crashed.note: What the message bar (under the toolbar) says when the page opens a machine whose tab closed while it ran (buttons to start it smaller follow): {{name}} is the machine's name, {{when}} when it was last seen running, {{gib}} and {{peak}} the memory it used then and at most (GiB), {{ram}} its RAM and {{jit}} its JIT cache (MiB).

memory-signal.crashed.jit.message: Start with a {{mib}} MiB JIT cache
memory-signal.crashed.jit.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the machine's tab closed while it ran: it starts the machine with a smaller JIT cache; {{mib}} is its size (160 or 64).

memory-signal.crashed.ram.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the machine's tab closed while it ran: it starts the machine with less RAM; {{mib}} is the RAM it gets.

memory-signal.crashed.asIs.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the machine's tab closed while it ran: it starts the machine unchanged.

memory-signal.memoryWarning.message: This needs about {{need}} GiB of memory, and your computer reports {{has}} GiB. If memory runs out, the browser will close the tab without warning.
memory-signal.memoryWarning.note: Paragraph after the question asked before a restart with another size (the toolbar's Machine menu, a stored machine's Save) when your computer may not have the memory: {{need}} is what the machine needs, {{has}} what your computer reports (GiB).

memory-signal.memoryWarning.after.note: A question asked before a restart with another size ({{question}}: the toolbar's Machine menu's, a stored machine's Save), with the paragraph that warns your computer may not have the memory ({{warning}}) after it, a blank line between them.

memory-signal.memoryWarning.max.message: This needs about {{need}} GiB of memory, and your computer reports {{has}} GiB. Browsers report at most 8 GiB, so it may have more. If memory runs out, the browser will close the tab without warning.
memory-signal.memoryWarning.max.note: Paragraph after the question asked before a restart with another size when your computer may not have the memory and reports 8 GiB, the most browsers report: {{need}} is what the machine needs, {{has}} what your computer reports (GiB).

size-actions.size_one.note: The size in the question “Restart with …?” (the toolbar's Machine menu) for one vCPU (a machine without a GPU): {{count}} is the vCPUs, {{ram}} the RAM in MiB.

size-actions.size_other.note: The size in the question “Restart with …?” (the toolbar's Machine menu) for several vCPUs (a machine without a GPU): {{count}} is the vCPUs, {{ram}} the RAM in MiB.

size-actions.size.3d_one.message: {{count}} vCPU, {{ram}} MiB of RAM and 3D graphics
size-actions.size.3d_one.note: The size in the question “Restart with …?” (the toolbar's Machine menu) for one vCPU with 3D graphics: {{count}} is the vCPUs, {{ram}} the RAM in MiB.

size-actions.size.3d_other.message: {{count}} vCPUs, {{ram}} MiB of RAM and 3D graphics
size-actions.size.3d_other.note: The size in the question “Restart with …?” (the toolbar's Machine menu) for several vCPUs with 3D graphics: {{count}} is the vCPUs, {{ram}} the RAM in MiB.

size-actions.size.2d_one.message: {{count}} vCPU, {{ram}} MiB of RAM and 2D graphics
size-actions.size.2d_one.note: The size in the question “Restart with …?” (the toolbar's Machine menu) for one vCPU with 2D graphics: {{count}} is the vCPUs, {{ram}} the RAM in MiB.

size-actions.size.2d_other.message: {{count}} vCPUs, {{ram}} MiB of RAM and 2D graphics
size-actions.size.2d_other.note: The size in the question “Restart with …?” (the toolbar's Machine menu) for several vCPUs with 2D graphics: {{count}} is the vCPUs, {{ram}} the RAM in MiB.

size-actions.size.confirm.message: Restart with {{size}}? If the machine is suspended, it will resume with the size it had, and the new size will apply from its next boot.
size-actions.size.confirm.note: Text of the question asked when a size is chosen in the toolbar's Machine menu while the machine isn't running; {{size}} is the size chosen (vCPUs, RAM, graphics).

size-actions.size.confirm.running.message: Restart with {{size}}? This will power off the machine immediately, like pulling the plug, and unsaved work in the guest will be lost.
size-actions.size.confirm.running.note: Text of the question asked when a size is chosen in the toolbar's Machine menu while the machine runs; {{size}} is the size chosen (vCPUs, RAM, graphics).

size-actions.size.title.note: Title of the question asked when a size is chosen in the toolbar's Machine menu.

size-actions.size.ok.note: The confirm button of the question asked when a size is chosen in the toolbar's Machine menu.

size-actions.settings.confirm.message: Restart <name>{{name}}</name> with its new settings? This will power it off immediately, like pulling the plug, and unsaved work in the guest will be lost.
size-actions.settings.confirm.note: Text of the question asked when the Home page's Settings tab saves new settings for the machine running on the page; {{name}} is the machine's name.

size-actions.settings.title.note: Title of the question asked when the Home page's Settings tab saves new settings for the machine running on the page.

size-actions.settings.ok.note: The confirm button (drawn as a warning) of the question asked when new settings are saved for the machine running on the page.

power-actions.notIsolated.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the page was served without the headers the emulator needs (nothing can run): the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (machine:main.notIsolated.cause).

power-actions.notIsolated.cause.message: This web app needs cross-origin isolation (the COOP and COEP headers) for the emulator's shared memory, and the server didn't send them.
power-actions.notIsolated.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:main.notIsolated, on the line under it in the message bar; why nothing can run.

power-actions.notIsolated.fix.message: Run `npm start` in the repository and open the URL it prints; its server sends them.
power-actions.notIsolated.fix.note: Error details: the line under machine:main.notIsolated.cause in the message bar; what to do (a development checkout served by another server).

memory-signal.memory_one.message:
This machine needs about {{need}} GiB of memory, counting {{ram}} MiB of guest RAM, {{count}} vCPU, and the emulator itself. Your computer reports {{has}} GiB.
{{advice}}
memory-signal.memory_one.note: What the message bar (under the toolbar) says before a start when your computer may not have the memory for the machine (Start anyway follows): {{need}} is what it needs and {{has}} what your computer reports (GiB), {{ram}} its RAM (MiB), {{count}} its vCPUs (one), {{advice}} what to do.

memory-signal.memory_other.message:
This machine needs about {{need}} GiB of memory, counting {{ram}} MiB of guest RAM, {{count}} vCPUs, and the emulator itself. Your computer reports {{has}} GiB.
{{advice}}
memory-signal.memory_other.note: What the message bar (under the toolbar) says before a start when your computer may not have the memory for the machine (Start anyway follows): {{need}} is what it needs and {{has}} what your computer reports (GiB), {{ram}} its RAM (MiB), {{count}} its vCPUs (several), {{advice}} what to do.

memory-signal.memory.max_one.message:
This machine needs about {{need}} GiB of memory, counting {{ram}} MiB of guest RAM, {{count}} vCPU, and the emulator itself. Your computer reports {{has}} GiB; browsers report at most 8 GiB, so it may have more.
{{advice}}
memory-signal.memory.max_one.note: What the message bar (under the toolbar) says before a start when your computer may not have the memory for the machine (Start anyway follows) and reports 8 GiB, the most browsers report: {{need}} is what it needs and {{has}} what your computer reports (GiB), {{ram}} its RAM (MiB), {{count}} its vCPUs (one), {{advice}} what to do.

memory-signal.memory.max_other.message:
This machine needs about {{need}} GiB of memory, counting {{ram}} MiB of guest RAM, {{count}} vCPUs, and the emulator itself. Your computer reports {{has}} GiB; browsers report at most 8 GiB, so it may have more.
{{advice}}
memory-signal.memory.max_other.note: What the message bar (under the toolbar) says before a start when your computer may not have the memory for the machine (Start anyway follows) and reports 8 GiB, the most browsers report: {{need}} is what it needs and {{has}} what your computer reports (GiB), {{ram}} its RAM (MiB), {{count}} its vCPUs (several), {{advice}} what to do.

memory-signal.memory.advice.message: If memory runs out, the browser closes the tab without warning. Close other tabs and apps first.
memory-signal.memory.advice.note: The advice line of the message bar's warning that your computer may not have the memory for the machine.

memory-signal.memory.advice.fewer.message: If memory runs out, the browser closes the tab without warning. Close other tabs and apps first, or use fewer vCPUs; {{fewer}} would fit (?ncpus={{fewer}}).
memory-signal.memory.advice.fewer.note: The advice line of the message bar's warning that your computer may not have the memory for the machine, when fewer vCPUs would fit; {{fewer}} is how many.

memory-signal.memory.start.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after the warning that your computer may not have the memory for the machine: it starts it all the same.

messages.noStorage.message: This browser doesn't let the web app keep anything (in a private window, for example): what the machine writes to its disks, its snapshots and the machines you make last only until this tab is closed.
messages.noStorage.note: Note in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the browser refuses the web app its storage (OPFS: Firefox's private windows), shown while there is nothing else to say. It takes the place of the note that the browser isn't Chromium.

messages.notChromium.message: This web app is developed and tested in Chromium and Chrome. In this browser, parts of it may not work.
messages.notChromium.note: Note in the message bar (under the toolbar) in a browser other than Chromium or Chrome, shown while there is nothing else to say.

worker-start.suspendedMachine.note: Names the machine kept suspended in this browser in the words of a snapshot that can't be loaded (in place of a file's name), inside a sentence (“Couldn't load the suspended machine”).

worker.notResumed.note: Note in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a start found a suspended machine that couldn't be resumed (the page boots the machine instead): the headline; what happened is the cause under it (machine:worker.notResumed.cause); why is the detail under it.

worker.notResumed.cause.message: Its suspended memory was discarded, and the machine is booting from its disk instead.
worker.notResumed.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker.notResumed, on the line under it in the same place; what happened.

worker-start.phase.resuming.note: Line on the boot card and the machine's state in the status bar while a start checks the machine kept suspended in this browser.

worker-start.diskChanged.message: Its disk has changed since it was suspended.
worker-start.diskChanged.note: Detail under “Couldn't resume the suspended machine” in the message bar (under the toolbar): a disk of the machine moved on since the suspend (a reset, a switch of overlay, a merge).

worker-start.vulkanSplit.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a machine with Vulkan has a memory split that leaves no room for Vulkan's memory (Retry follows): the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (machine:worker-start.vulkanSplit.cause, or machine:worker-start.vulkanSplit.snapshot.cause for a snapshot); {{machine}} is the machine's name, {{why}} what is wrong with the split (a machines catalog message, lower case).

worker-start.vulkanSplit.cause.message: Its memory split doesn't work with Vulkan ({{why}}). Change the machine's memory on the <ui-home>Home</ui-home> page, or the split in the address, or turn Vulkan off for it.
worker-start.vulkanSplit.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-start.vulkanSplit, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{why}}: as that entry's note says. The <ui-home> marker shows the Home button's icon before its words.

worker-start.vulkanSplit.snapshot.cause.message: The snapshot's memory split doesn't work with Vulkan ({{why}}). Turn Vulkan off for the machine, or start it without the snapshot.
worker-start.vulkanSplit.snapshot.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-start.vulkanSplit when a snapshot loaded on a machine with Vulkan has a memory split that leaves no room for Vulkan's memory; why and what to do. {{why}} is what is wrong with the split (a machines catalog message, lower case).

worker.panic.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the guest's kernel panicked (Show serial log and the like follow); the kernel's panic line is the detail under it, after its cause (machine:worker.panic.cause) on the line under the headline.

worker.panic.cause.message: The serial log shows what led to it. <ui-refresh>Restart</ui-refresh> boots the machine again.
worker.panic.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker.panic, on the line under it in the same place; what happened. <ui-refresh>Restart</ui-refresh> is the toolbar's Restart button, drawn with its icon.

worker.resumed.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) once a suspended machine was resumed; it closes itself after a while.

worker.stopped.unimplemented.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the guest used something the emulator doesn't have (Show serial log and the like follow): the headline; why is the cause under it (machine:worker.stopped.unimplemented.cause); {{pc}} is the address, in hex.

worker.stopped.unimplemented.cause.message: The guest used an instruction or register that $t(common:product.name) doesn't implement (at pc 0x{{pc}}).
worker.stopped.unimplemented.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker.stopped.unimplemented, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. {{pc}}: as that entry's note says.

worker.stopped.exit.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the emulator stopped for a reason it has no words for; {{exit}} is its exit code.

worker-fetch.http.note: What the server answered for a file the machine needs, in the error that it's missing (“The server answered … for …”); {{status}} is the HTTP status.

worker-fetch.http.notFound.note: What the server answered for a file the machine needs when it isn't there, in the error that it's missing (“The server answered … for …”); {{status}} is the HTTP status (404).

worker-fetch.noCore.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the emulator's core can't be fetched from the server (a development checkout; Retry follows): the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (machine:worker-fetch.noCore.cause); {{path}} is its path in the repository, {{why}} what the server answered (HTTP and its status).

worker-fetch.noCore.cause.message: The server answered {{why}} for {{path}}, so the core may not be built. Run `npm start` in the repository; it builds the core, then serves this web app.
worker-fetch.noCore.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-fetch.noCore, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{why}}, {{path}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-fetch.noImage.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a file of a test machine can't be fetched from the server (Retry follows): the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (machine:worker-fetch.noImage.cause); {{machine}} is the machine's name, {{path}} the file's path in the repository, {{why}} what the server answered (HTTP and its status), {{prepare}} the command that builds it.

worker-fetch.noImage.cause.message: The server answered {{why}} for {{path}}. Run {{prepare}}, then <ui>Retry</ui>.
worker-fetch.noImage.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-fetch.noImage, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{why}}, {{path}}, {{prepare}}: as that entry's note says. <ui>Retry</ui> is the message bar's button (machine:problems.retry).

worker-fetch.noServer.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the server didn't answer for a file the machine needs (Retry follows): the headline; what to check is the cause under it (machine:worker-fetch.noServer.cause); {{path}} is the file's path in the repository; the browser's error is the detail under it.

worker-fetch.noServer.cause.message: The server didn't answer. Check that it is still running (`npm start`).
worker-fetch.noServer.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-fetch.noServer, on the line under it in the same place; what to check.

worker-errors.diskInUse.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the machine's disk is open in another tab (Retry follows): the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (machine:worker-errors.diskInUse.cause); {{machine}} is the machine's name; the lower-level error is the detail under it.

worker-errors.diskInUse.cause.message: Another tab or window of this web app is running the machine on the same disk, and the browser lets only one of them open it at a time. Close that tab, then <ui>Retry</ui>.
worker-errors.diskInUse.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-errors.diskInUse, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. <ui>Retry</ui> is the message bar's button (machine:problems.retry).

worker-errors.diskMerging.cause.message: An overlay is being merged into one of the machine's disks. Wait for the merge to finish, then <ui>Retry</ui>.
worker-errors.diskMerging.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-errors.diskInUse, on the line under it in the same place, when the start found a merge (Merge into the disk, in this tab or another) under way into one of the machine's stored disks: the start is refused rather than open an overlay the merge is deleting. <ui>Retry</ui> is the message bar's button (machine:problems.retry).

worker-errors.diskMismatch.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the changes kept for the machine's disk were made over another image (Reset disk… or Disks… follows): the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (machine:worker-errors.diskMismatch.cause); {{machine}} is the machine's name; the lower-level error is the detail under it.

worker-errors.diskMismatch.cause.message: The changes kept for its disk were made over a different image than the one served now. To start over from this image, reset the disk, which deletes those changes.
worker-errors.diskMismatch.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-errors.diskMismatch, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do.

worker-errors.memory.message: Couldn't reserve memory for the machine
worker-errors.memory.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the browser refused the machine's memory (Retry follows): the headline; what to do is the cause under it (machine:worker-errors.memory.cause); {{ram}} is the RAM; the browser's error is the detail under it.

worker-errors.memory.cause.message: The browser refused {{ram}} MiB for the machine's RAM. Close other tabs, then <ui>Retry</ui>.
worker-errors.memory.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-errors.memory, on the line under it in the same place; what to do. {{ram}}: as that entry's note says. <ui>Retry</ui> is the message bar's button (machine:problems.retry).

worker-errors.emulator.message: The emulator stopped with an error
worker-errors.emulator.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the emulator failed (Show serial log and the like follow); the error and where it happened (for a bug report) are the details under it.

worker-snapshot.suspend.notRunning.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when Suspend reached a machine that had already stopped: the headline; why is the cause under it (machine:worker-snapshot.suspend.notRunning.cause).

worker-snapshot.suspend.notRunning.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-snapshot.suspend.notRunning, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything.

worker-snapshot.suspend.noHome.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when Suspend is asked of a machine that keeps nothing in this browser: the headline; why is the cause under it (machine:worker-snapshot.suspend.noHome.cause).

worker-snapshot.suspend.noHome.cause.message: Only a machine whose disk changes are kept in this browser can be suspended.
worker-snapshot.suspend.noHome.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-snapshot.suspend.noHome, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything.

worker-snapshot.suspend.busy.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when Suspend is asked while a snapshot is being written: the headline; what to do is the cause under it (machine:worker-snapshot.suspend.busy.cause).

worker-snapshot.suspend.busy.cause.message: A snapshot is being saved. Suspend the machine once it's done.
worker-snapshot.suspend.busy.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machine:worker-snapshot.suspend.busy, on the line under it in the same place; what to do.

worker-snapshot.phase.suspending.note: The machine's state in the status bar while Suspend writes its memory (a percentage may follow).

worker-snapshot.suspended.message: The machine is suspended, and its memory ({{size, bytes}}) is kept in this browser. <ui>Start</ui> resumes it where it was. <ui>Boot instead</ui> starts it from its disk, as after a power cut.
worker-snapshot.suspended.note: Note in the message bar (under the toolbar) once the machine was suspended (Start and Boot instead follow); {{size}} is what its memory takes in this browser. The markers frame the message bar's buttons' words (machine:problems.resume, machine:problems.bootInstead).

worker-snapshot.suspend.failed.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when Suspend failed (the machine runs on); why is the detail under it.

soft-power.refused.off.message: The guest refused to shut down: a program is holding it off.
soft-power.refused.off.note: Message bar notice when the toolbar's Power off asked the guest to shut down and the guest refused (a program inhibits it, e.g. a running update). The page then asks whether to power off at once.

soft-power.refused.reboot.message: The guest refused to restart: a program is holding it off.
soft-power.refused.reboot.note: Message bar notice when the toolbar's Restart asked the guest to restart and the guest refused (a program inhibits it). The page then asks whether to restart at once.

soft-power.busy.message: The guest is still working on an earlier request to shut down or restart.
soft-power.busy.note: Message bar notice when the toolbar's Power off or Restart asked the guest while an earlier request (one the page gave up waiting for) still runs in it. The page then asks whether to power off or restart at once.

soft-power.noAnswer.message: The guest didn't answer the request to shut down or restart.
soft-power.noAnswer.note: Message bar notice when the toolbar's Power off or Restart asked the guest (through its agent, the page's program in the guest) and no answer came within 15 seconds. The page then asks whether to power off or restart at once.

soft-power.noTool.message: The guest has no way to shut itself down that the page knows.
soft-power.noTool.note: Message bar notice when the toolbar's Power off or Restart asked the guest and its agent found neither systemd-logind nor the shutdown command. The page then asks whether to power off or restart at once.

power-actions.shuttingDown.message: The guest is shutting down. The change goes on once it has powered off.
power-actions.shuttingDown.note: Text of the dialog shown while the guest shuts down before a change on the Home page (a disk's export, new settings, another machine opened, an edit that needs the machine off), when the guest's agent (the page's program in the guest) asked it to. It closes by itself once the guest powered off.

power-actions.shuttingDown.title.note: Title of the dialog shown while the guest shuts down before a change on the Home page.

power-actions.shuttingDown.now.note: The one button (drawn as a warning) of the dialog shown while the guest shuts down: it powers the machine off at once, like pulling the plug, without waiting for the guest.

disk-actions.switch.confirm.soft.message: Open <name>{{machine}}</name>? The guest of <name>{{running}}</name> will be asked to shut down first; you will be able to power it off forcibly, if needed.
disk-actions.switch.confirm.soft.note: Text of the question asked before opening another machine while this one runs, when its guest's agent (the page's program in the guest) can shut it down cleanly. {{machine}} is the name of the machine to open, {{running}} is the name of the machine running in this tab.

size-actions.settings.confirm.soft.message: Restart <name>{{name}}</name> with its new settings? Its guest will be asked to shut down first; you will be able to power it off forcibly, if needed.
size-actions.settings.confirm.soft.note: Text of the question asked by the Settings tab's Save and restart while the machine runs, when its guest's agent can shut it down cleanly. {{name}} is the machine's name.

power-actions.shuttingDown.refused.message: The guest didn't shut down (the message bar says why). Power off the machine now, like pulling the plug? Unsaved work in the guest will be lost. <ui>Cancel</ui> keeps it running, and the change isn't made.
power-actions.shuttingDown.refused.note: Question asked before a change on the Home page (a disk's export, new settings, another machine opened, an edit that needs the machine off) when the guest was asked to shut down and refused or didn't answer. <ui>Cancel</ui> is the question's own button (common:ask.cancel).

RamWindow.title.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it). The window's title.

RamWindow.reading.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it). In place of the map until the first look at the RAM is done; and the line under the map while another run's RAM is looked at, the map before dimmed meanwhile.

RamWindow.scale.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it). Over the map: how much of the RAM each square is. {{size}} is a size (4 MiB, 16 MiB, 1 GiB): a larger window has smaller squares.

RamWindow.live_one.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it). Over the map, beside a green light: how often the map looks at the RAM again ({{count}} seconds, at least 1). A larger RAM takes longer to look at, so it is looked at less often.

RamWindow.live_other.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it). Over the map, beside a green light: how often the map looks at the RAM again ({{count}} seconds). A larger RAM takes longer to look at, so it is looked at less often.

RamWindow.live.title.message: The map looks at the RAM again and again while the machine runs, as often as it can while taking little of the computer's time. It doesn't show the guest's reads and writes, only what changed between two looks.
RamWindow.live.title.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it). The tooltip of the "Updated every … seconds" sign over the map.

RamWindow.map.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it). The spoken name of the map (a grid of squares; the arrow keys move between them, Enter pins one).

RamWindow.pinned.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the pinned square's details, in a small window of its own beside the map after a click on a square. The window's title.

RamDetails.prev.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the pinned square's details, in a small window of its own beside the map after a click on a square. A square that covers several ranges of 4 MiB: the tooltip and spoken name of the left arrow button that shows the range before.

RamDetails.next.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the pinned square's details, in a small window of its own beside the map after a click on a square. A square that covers several ranges of 4 MiB: the tooltip and spoken name of the right arrow button that shows the range after.

RamDetails.step.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the pinned square's details, in a small window of its own beside the map after a click on a square. A square that covers several ranges of 4 MiB: between the arrow buttons, which of the square's {{count}} ranges is shown ({{at}}, from 1).

RamDetails.pages.message: Pages of 4 KiB in this range
RamDetails.pages.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the pinned square's details, in a small window of its own beside the map after a click on a square. The spoken name of the small map of the range's 1,024 pages of 4 KiB (32 by 32).

ram-source.notRunning.message: The RAM map shows the RAM of a machine running in this tab. Start the machine to see it.
ram-source.notRunning.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it), in place of the map: no machine runs in this tab (it stopped, or hasn't started).

ram-source.noAnswer.message: Looking at the RAM took too long.
ram-source.noAnswer.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it), in place of the map: the running machine didn't answer in time. The map asks again.

ram-look.legend.zero.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the legend under the map, beside a square drawn as the map draws it. A square whose part of the RAM holds only zeros: memory the guest never wrote, or gave back.

ram-look.legend.some.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the legend under the map, beside a square drawn as the map draws it. A square with some pages that hold data (anything but zeros: the faintest of four shades, any page at all).

ram-look.legend.full.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the legend under the map, beside a square drawn as the map draws it. A square whose every page holds data (the strongest shade).

ram-look.legend.changed.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the legend under the map, beside a square drawn as the map draws it. A square with an inner square: pages there changed between the map's last two looks at the RAM (in four shades of how many).

ram-look.legend.cleared.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the legend under the map, beside a square drawn as the map draws it. A square with a hollow inner square: pages there held data at the look before and only zeros now (memory the guest freed and gave back, or zeroed), and none changed otherwise.

ram-look.at.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. Where the square (or the range) is in the guest's physical address space: {{from}} and {{to}} are hexadecimal addresses (0x4000_0000), {{to}} the address just past its end.

ram-look.data_one.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. How many of its {{count}} pages of 4 KiB hold anything but zeros ({{data}}). Used only for a single page.

ram-look.data_other.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. How many of its {{count}} pages of 4 KiB hold anything but zeros ({{data}}).

ram-look.zero_one.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. None of its pages of 4 KiB holds data. Used only for a single page.

ram-look.zero_other.message: All its {{count}} pages hold only zeros.
ram-look.zero_other.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. None of its {{count}} pages of 4 KiB holds data: memory the guest never wrote, or gave back.

ram-look.unchanged.message: Nothing changed since the last look.
ram-look.unchanged.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. From the map's second look at the RAM on: none of its pages changed between the last two looks.

ram-look.changed_one.message: 1 page changed since the last look.
ram-look.changed_one.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. From the map's second look at the RAM on: how many of its pages ({{count}}) hold other data than at the look before.

ram-look.changed_other.message: {{count}} pages changed since the last look.
ram-look.changed_other.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. From the map's second look at the RAM on: how many of its pages ({{count}}) hold other data than at the look before.

ram-look.cleared_one.message: 1 page was cleared since the last look.
ram-look.cleared_one.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. From the map's second look at the RAM on: how many of its pages ({{count}}) held data at the look before and only zeros now (memory the guest freed and gave back, or zeroed).

ram-look.cleared_other.message: {{count}} pages were cleared since the last look.
ram-look.cleared_other.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer (or the keyboard's cursor) is on a square, which tells that square's numbers; also the first sentences of the pinned square's details (one range of 4 MiB, page by page). One of its sentences. From the map's second look at the RAM on: how many of its pages ({{count}}) held data at the look before and only zeros now (memory the guest freed and gave back, or zeroed).

ram-look.whole.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer is on no square, which tells what the RAM holds as a whole. One of its sentences. {{size}} is how much of the RAM's pages hold anything but zeros, {{total}} the RAM's size. Memory the guest frees keeps its data until the guest gives it back.

ram-look.wholeChanged.message: {{size, bytes}} changed and {{cleared, bytes}} were cleared since the last look.
ram-look.wholeChanged.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer is on no square, which tells what the RAM holds as a whole. One of its sentences. From the map's second look on: {{size}} is how much of the RAM holds other data than at the look before, {{cleared}} how much held data then and only zeros now.

ram-look.firstLook.message: Changes show from the next look.
ram-look.firstLook.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer is on no square, which tells what the RAM holds as a whole. One of its sentences. Only after the map's first look at the RAM: what changed is known from the second.

ram-look.hint.message: Point at a square to see what it holds. Click it to see its pages.
ram-look.hint.note: The RAM map (a floating window opened by clicking RAM in the status bar while the machine runs in this tab: the running machine's RAM as a grid of squares, each a part of it): the line under the map while the pointer is on no square, which tells what the RAM holds as a whole. One of its sentences. Its last sentence: how to use the map.

vm.ramTooSmall.message: The machine's RAM is too small for its boot files
vm.ramTooSmall.note: Error headline in the message bar when a machine is started with less RAM than its firmware, kernel or initial ramdisk need where they are loaded (a size set by hand in the page's address, ?ram=). Its details: vm.ramTooSmall.need.

vm.ramTooSmall.need.message: They need {{need, bytes}} of RAM, and the machine has {{ram, bytes}}.
vm.ramTooSmall.need.note: Details under the error headline vm.ramTooSmall (the machine's RAM is too small for its boot files): {{need}} is the RAM its firmware, kernel or initial ramdisk need where they are loaded, {{ram}} the machine's RAM.
